name: Freedom House
tagline: Freedom on the Net: the benchmark annual assessment of global internet freedom
description: Founded in 1941, Freedom House is one of the oldest US democracy watchdogs, best known for its Freedom in the World ratings. Its core technology workstream is Freedom on the Net (FOTN), an annual report scoring internet freedom in ~70 countries covering roughly 88% of the world's internet users. FOTN has made AI a central theme: the 2023 edition, 'The Repressive Power of Artificial Intelligence,' documented how governments use AI to enhance censorship, surveillance, and disinformation; the 2024 edition ('The Struggle for Trust Online') tracked generative AI in a record election year; and 2025 ('An Uncertain Future for the Global Internet') found AI compounding a 15th consecutive year of decline. The reports pair country narratives with numerical scores used by policymakers, journalists, and researchers worldwide.
aiDemocracyAngle: Freedom on the Net is the definitive annual index of how AI-driven censorship, surveillance, and generative disinformation erode internet freedom and democratic discourse.

keyProjects.name: Freedom on the Net
keyProjects.note: Annual internet-freedom index; 2023 edition focused on AI repression

name: Future of Life Institute
tagline: Advocacy and grants against AI-driven power concentration
description: The Future of Life Institute (FLI) is a nonprofit founded in 2014 that works to reduce large-scale risks from transformative technologies, especially AI. Beyond its well-known open letters and policy advocacy, FLI has made mitigating AI-driven power concentration an explicit pillar: it ran a grant program (~$4M, 13 projects funded) to counter concentrated control and preserve meaningful human agency, spanning technical interventions, a risk index for authoritarian AI, and investigative journalism on AI in politics. FLI warns that advanced AI could enable Orwellian surveillance, discourse manipulation and 'truth decay' that erode democratic participation. Its 'Keep the Future Human' essay and AI Action Plan recommendations argue for governance that prevents power over AI, and power exercised via AI, from collapsing into a few corporate or state hands. FLI is both a research/advocacy organization and, through its grants, a funder in this space.
aiDemocracyAngle: Funds and campaigns specifically against AI-enabled power concentration and authoritarian AI, framing it as a direct threat to democratic participation.

name: The Future Society
tagline: Aligning AI through better governance
description: The Future Society (TFS) is an independent nonprofit founded in 2014 (incubated at Harvard Kennedy School, incorporated as a US 501(c)(3) in 2016) that works to align AI through better governance. Its distributed team, based across a dozen countries, helps US, EU and global decision-makers design and implement AI governance mechanisms: laws, regulations, standards and voluntary frameworks. Themes include US AI governance, European AI governance (including EU AI Act implementation) and global AI governance, with a focus since 2023 on risks in the research and development of advanced AI. TFS convenes the Athens Roundtable on AI and the Rule of Law, runs educational programs, and partners with more than 60 institutions including the OECD, UNESCO and the Future of Life Institute. Its democratic relevance lies in embedding rule-of-law, fundamental-freedoms and accountability principles into how powerful AI is regulated.
aiDemocracyAngle: Shapes the laws, standards and institutions governing advanced AI so they protect rule of law, fundamental freedoms and democratic accountability.

keyProjects.name: International & European AI Governance
keyProjects.note: AI Act and international governance work

name: g0v (gov-zero)
tagline: Decentralized Taiwanese civic-tech community that 'forks' government
description: g0v (pronounced 'gov-zero') is a decentralized, volunteer-driven civic-tech community founded in Taiwan in 2012, built on core values of information transparency, open source, and open collaboration. Its name replaces the 'o' in 'gov' with a zero, signaling a reimagining of government from scratch. g0v's model is to 'fork' government: taking official datasets, services, and information and rebuilding them in the open with better usability, transparency, and accessibility. It operates primarily online with large hackathons roughly every two months where participants propose projects and recruit volunteers; since 2012 it has hosted 40+ hackathons, four international summits, and multiple civic-tech grant rounds, drawing over 8,000 contributors globally. g0v incubated vTaiwan and many civic tools (including the Cofacts fact-checking chatbot), and became an important force in Taiwan's democracy and the global civic-tech movement. It is the grassroots engine from which much of Taiwan's celebrated digital-democracy tooling emerged.
aiDemocracyAngle: g0v is the open-source community incubator behind Taiwan's digital-democracy tools, including AI-adjacent projects like fact-checking bots and the vTaiwan process.

name: Global Disinformation Index
tagline: Tracks and disrupts the monetisation of disinformation: risk ratings plus economic research
description: The Global Disinformation Index (GDI) is a UK-based not-for-profit founded in 2018 by Clare Melford and Daniel Rogers that works to disrupt the business model of disinformation. GDI has combined AI and expert human review to produce independent, neutral disinformation risk ratings for news and information sites worldwide, and today emphasizes mapping and disrupting the economic flows that monetise disinformation. It connects these ratings into programmatic ad-buying networks so brands, agencies, and ad-tech firms can avoid unintentionally funding sites that spread harmful narratives, a challenge intensified by AI-generated 'made for advertising' websites. GDI operates on principles of neutrality, independence, and transparency.
aiDemocracyAngle: GDI uses AI plus human review to rate the disinformation risk of thousands of sites and cut off their ad revenue, countering the rise of AI-generated 'made-for-advertising' disinformation.

name: The GovLab (The Governance Lab)
tagline: Governing more effectively through technology, data, and collective intelligence
description: The Governance Lab (The GovLab), founded in 2012 by Beth Simone Noveck (originally at NYU Tandon, now affiliated with Northeastern University), works to deepen understanding of how to govern more effectively and legitimately through technology, data, and collective intelligence. Its projects include CrowdLaw (methods and platforms for citizen participation in lawmaking), Data Collaboratives (public-value data sharing), Responsible Data for Children, the GovLab Academy, and the Living Library. Increasingly it focuses on AI and democracy through the Reboot Democracy blog and research on how artificial intelligence and collective intelligence can strengthen democratic institutions. The GovLab both studies and prototypes participatory governance, running experiments with governments worldwide and training public professionals. Under Noveck, New Jersey's first Chief AI Strategist, it is a leading academic-practitioner hub for using technology to make democratic institutions more open, participatory, and evidence-driven.
aiDemocracyAngle: The GovLab pioneered 'CrowdLaw' and now leads Reboot Democracy: research and tools for using AI and collective intelligence to make democratic institutions more participatory and effective.

name: Gradual Disempowerment (research project)
tagline: The seminal paper reframing AI x-risk as slow, systemic human disempowerment
description: 'Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development' is a widely cited 2025 research project and paper (with its own site) by Jan Kulveit, Raymond Douglas, Nora Ammann, Deger Turan, David Krueger and David Duvenaud. It reframes AI existential risk away from sudden takeover toward a slower dynamic: as AI increasingly substitutes for human labor and cognition in markets, culture and government, the feedback loops that keep those systems responsive to human interests weaken, potentially producing an irreversible loss of human influence. The authors stress that societal systems currently rely on humans to function, which implicitly aligns them with human welfare; automation severs that link. The project spans institutions including ACS Research (Charles University), Telic Research, ARIA, the AI Objectives Institute, Metaculus, Mila and the University of Toronto, and has become a central reference point for later work on structural AI risk and power concentration.
aiDemocracyAngle: Argues that voting, consumer choice and other democratic control levers lose force as AI displaces the human participation that once made states and markets serve people.

name: Harvard Ash Center — Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation & GETTING-Plurality
tagline: Danielle Allen's lab renovating democracy for the age of emerging technology
description: The Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation, based at Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center and led by political philosopher Danielle Allen, works to renovate democratic institutions for the 21st century under a framework of 'power-sharing liberalism,' treating democracy as a standard that shapes all policymaking rather than a stand-alone domain. Housed alongside it is the GETTING-Plurality research network (Governance of Emerging Technology and Technology Innovations for Next-Generation Governance), which links philosophers, social scientists, computer scientists, legal scholars, and technologists studying how emerging technology, including AI, should be governed and how it can be built to respect pluralism and diverse human intelligence. The network advances a 'plurality' framework for technology development, produces roadmaps on technology governance and power-sharing liberalism, and runs fellowships. It is a leading academic center connecting political theory to concrete design of AI-era democratic institutions and tools.
aiDemocracyAngle: GETTING-Plurality shapes how emerging technology and AI are governed and designed for pluralism, translating democratic theory into technology-governance standards.

name: Hewlett Foundation
tagline: Funds security of emerging tech and democracy-geopolitics of AI
description: The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, endowed by HP co-founder William Hewlett's fortune, ran a time-limited Cyber Initiative (2014-2023, initially $65M) that in its final years concentrated on the intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It has continued into emerging-technology security: in February 2026 it announced $10M in exploratory grants on the intersection of national security and frontier technologies, including $2.5M each to Stanford's Hoover Institution and Vanderbilt University. Its grantees include Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CyberAI Project), the Institute for Security and Technology's Democracy and the Geopolitics of Technology practice, and Vanderbilt's Wicked Problems Lab, which is building a synthetic-information filtering testbed to study AI-driven persuasion and build resilience against synthetic information warfare. While Hewlett is a large general-purpose foundation rather than an AI-democracy specialist, its emerging-tech-security portfolio explicitly funds work on AI's implications for democratic resilience, information integrity, and geopolitical stability.
aiDemocracyAngle: Funds work on AI-driven persuasion, synthetic information warfare, and the democracy-geopolitics of technology as threats to democratic resilience.

name: Humanity AI
tagline: $500M philanthropic coalition steering AI toward the public good
description: Humanity AI is a collaborative philanthropic initiative launched in October 2025 by a coalition of major US foundations, committing $500 million over five years to ensure AI development is shaped by and for people rather than driven solely by profit. Its founding partners include the Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Mellon Foundation, Mozilla Foundation, Omidyar Network, David and Lucile Packard Foundation, Doris Duke Foundation, Lumina Foundation, Kapor Foundation and Siegel Family Endowment. The initiative organizes its grantmaking around priority areas of Democracy, Education, Humanities and Culture, Labor and Economy, and Security. The democracy pillar funds new partnerships and frameworks for AI to advance and protect democratic rights and freedoms. In May 2026 it announced more than $18 million in pooled grants, including inaugural grantees (such as Data & Society's AI Civics program) and an open call. It aims to amplify public voice in AI's future.
aiDemocracyAngle: Pools half a billion dollars of foundation funding, with a dedicated democracy pillar, to back organizations advancing and protecting democracy in the AI era.

name: Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD)
tagline: Threat intelligence on disinformation and AI-enabled influence ops
description: The Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD) is an independent nonprofit founded in 2006 with offices in London, Berlin, Paris, Washington DC, Toronto and Amman. It combines data-driven analysis, policy advice and operational programs to counter extremism, hate, polarization and disinformation. A world leader in exposing Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), ISD tracks pro-Kremlin, pro-Beijing and other coordinated influence networks. Its recent research documents how AI is used in elections: ahead of the 2024 US vote it found 154 pieces of unlabelled AI-generated or manipulated election content that drew over 51 million impressions, and it assessed AI-driven manipulation in Germany's 2025 federal election. ISD also studies how users misidentify authentic content as AI-generated (in 52% of cases in one study), and advises platforms and governments on countermeasures and digital-literacy programs.
aiDemocracyAngle: Detects and exposes how AI-generated content and foreign influence operations distort elections and public debate across platforms.

keyProjects.note: Ongoing tracking of AI-enabled election manipulation

name: Integrity Institute
tagline: Trust & safety professionals building a better social internet
description: The Integrity Institute is a nonprofit think tank founded in 2021 by former Facebook integrity workers Jeff Allen and Sahar Massachi. It is powered by more than 450 integrity professionals who have worked on trust, safety and content moderation at platforms including Facebook, Google, X, TikTok, Discord and WhatsApp, and who pool their expertise to help platforms and regulators design healthier online systems. Its Elections Integrity Program (launched with Knight Foundation support) produces practical guidance, including a Global Elections Playbook: AI Edition, and analyses of foreign influence operations across the 2020 and 2024 US elections. The Institute researches recommender systems, generative-AI harms and platform design, and translates insider knowledge into concrete recommendations for platform governance and regulation. It offers a rare practitioner-grounded perspective on how AI and platform design affect elections and public discourse.
aiDemocracyAngle: Channels ex-platform insiders' expertise into concrete election-integrity and AI-safety guidance for social media companies and regulators.
funders: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation

keyProjects.note: Research on influence ops and platform design

name: The Intelligence Curse
tagline: Essay series: when AI makes labor irrelevant, elites stop needing people
description: The Intelligence Curse is an essay series (intelligence-curse.ai) by Luke Drago and Rudolf Laine arguing that transformative AI could sever the economic link between powerful actors and ordinary people. Drawing an analogy to the 'resource curse,' they contend that once AI makes human labor economically irrelevant, states and firms lose their incentive to invest in, protect, or listen to their populations, concentrating power and risking mass disempowerment. The series proposes a three-part response: avert catastrophes, diffuse AI capabilities broadly to individuals, and democratize the institutions that govern the transition. The project seeded Workshop Labs, a public-benefit startup the authors founded to build user-owned, personalized AI; in 2026 Workshop Labs joined Thinking Machines, where the founders continue their 'keep the future human' mission. The essays remain an influential reference in debates over AI, economic power and democratic accountability.
aiDemocracyAngle: Frames AI-driven power concentration as economics: when labor stops mattering, elites stop needing the public, undermining the material basis of democratic bargaining.

name: interface (formerly Stiftung Neue Verantwortung)
tagline: Berlin tech-policy think tank on platform regulation and the digital public sphere
description: interface, the Berlin nonprofit think tank founded in 2008 as Stiftung Neue Verantwortung (SNV) and renamed in 2024, specializes in technology's effect on society, combining data analysis with political analysis to inform German and European policy. One of its core programs, 'Strengthening the Digital Public Sphere and Platform Regulation,' shapes European debates on regulating large online platforms, focusing on risk assessment, transparency, and accountability under the EU Digital Services Act and national law. Its research has long addressed disinformation and its threats to democracy, including the 'Measuring Disinformation' project, and covers AI's role in the information ecosystem, surveillance, and digital rights.
aiDemocracyAngle: interface develops the platform-regulation and transparency frameworks (notably under the EU DSA) needed to hold AI-driven recommender systems and disinformation to account.

name: International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES)
tagline: Election-assistance body with an Information Integrity practice tackling AI disinfo
description: IFES (founded 1987) is a leading global provider of election assistance, supporting electoral management bodies and civil society in more than 145 countries. Its Cyber & Information Integrity expertise area runs an Information Integrity program that counters disinformation, misinformation, and dangerous speech while strengthening election authorities' communications. On AI, IFES published 'Brave New Ballot,' examining global uses of generative AI in campaigns and political communication and offering recommendations for election authorities, and developed the Chain of Harm Framework mapping how online falsehoods move through information ecosystems. In Kenya it built a custom AI-based hate-speech monitoring tool (in English, Kiswahili, and Sheng) with the national election commission.
aiDemocracyAngle: IFES's Information Integrity program and 'Brave New Ballot' report help election authorities manage generative-AI disinformation, and it fields AI monitoring tools like its Kenya hate-speech dashboard.

keyProjects.note: Counters disinformation and strengthens EMB communications

name: International IDEA
tagline: Intergovernmental body building electoral resilience for the AI era
description: The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance is an intergovernmental organization (34 member states) that supports elections and democratic institutions globally and publishes the Global State of Democracy report. It runs a dedicated Artificial Intelligence theme spanning research, standards, and capacity-building. Its flagship AI program, 'AI for Electoral Actors,' supported by Microsoft and OpenAI, ran a first global workshop series in 2025 to build AI literacy and resilience among electoral management bodies, civil society, and media. IDEA has published reports on AI in electoral management, using AI to strengthen political-finance oversight (case studies in Lithuania, Mexico, UK), and 'Safeguarding Democracy' on the nexus of elections, information integrity, and AI. It also studies information pollution across 2024 elections in Bangladesh, Ghana, Indonesia, Mexico, Mongolia, Pakistan, and South Africa.
aiDemocracyAngle: Through 'AI for Electoral Actors' and its AI theme, IDEA equips election commissions and civil society to manage generative-AI risks while responsibly adopting AI in electoral administration.

name: International Republican Institute (IRI)
tagline: Nonpartisan democracy-support group: elections, governance, countering authoritarian influence
description: IRI (founded 1983, nonpartisan democracy-support organization) works on governance, elections, and countering authoritarian influence globally. Its flagship technology-and-democracy workstream was the Beacon Project, launched in 2015 and run from IRI's Brussels office, which used data-driven media monitoring to expose and counter Russian and other foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) in Europe. Beacon developed a media-monitoring tool called '>versus<' shared with local partners, trained ~200 analysts across European civil society, and supported 130+ research publications, including a seven-country FIMI report series. IRI also runs broader technology-and-democracy programming addressing digital authoritarianism and the information environment.
aiDemocracyAngle: The Beacon Project applied data analytics and its '>versus<' monitoring tool to detect foreign information manipulation, increasingly AI-generated, targeting European democracies.

name: iSideWith
tagline: Most-taken US political quiz matching voters to candidates and parties
description: iSideWith is a popular US-based political quiz and voter guide launched in March 2012 by Taylor Peck and Nick Boutelier, independent of any party, investor or interest group. Users answer questions on political issues, weight the ones they care about, and are shown percentage matches with candidates, parties and other users. Its matching algorithm factors in 'passion' (how often a candidate raises an issue, whether it's a priority) and 'confidence' (how long a stance has been held and whether the voting record affirms it). Covering local, state and national US races, and expanded to other countries, it has been taken by tens of millions of people and is widely used in classrooms as a civics tool. It is a classic questionnaire quiz rather than an AI system.
aiDemocracyAngle: The most widely taken US political-quiz VAA, a mass-scale reference for issue-based candidate matching without AI.

name: Iswe Foundation
tagline: Catalyzing a global shift to participatory systems and a Global Citizens' Assembly
description: Iswe Foundation is an independent innovation center working with communities, movements, governments, and institutions to catalyze a global shift toward participatory political systems fit for the future. Its most prominent initiative is co-founding the Global Citizens' Assembly for People and Planet, developed alongside governments, civil-society organizations, researchers, and UN partners. The model pairs a demographically representative 'core assembly' of around 300 people selected by civic lottery with thousands of local community assemblies that feed grassroots experience into international policymaking, with an ambition to reach over ten million people by 2030. Launched with support from the Government of Brazil and oriented toward COP30 climate ambition, the Assembly seeks to give ordinary people, including those on the frontlines of climate change, a real voice in global decisions. Iswe builds the connective infrastructure for global deliberation; AI and digital tools are enablers for coordinating participation at planetary scale rather than its central focus.
aiDemocracyAngle: Iswe's global assembly relies on digital and AI-supported infrastructure to link thousands of local assemblies and synthesize input across languages at planetary scale.

name: Jigsaw (Google)
tagline: Google incubator building tech to counter disinformation and online threats
description: Jigsaw is a unit within Google, created in 2010 (as Google Ideas, renamed Jigsaw in 2016), that builds technology to give people greater agency against online threats including disinformation, censorship, harassment and cyberattacks. Its democracy-relevant products are widely used by civil society. Project Shield offers free enterprise-grade DDoS protection to independent media, election-monitoring groups and human-rights organizations so they stay online during sensitive periods. Its prebunking program, grounded in inoculation psychology, runs short videos that teach people to recognize manipulation techniques before they encounter them; campaigns have reached tens of millions of voters in Europe, Indonesia and elsewhere, often with local election commissions. Perspective API uses machine learning to help platforms moderate toxic content and support healthier civic conversation, and Jigsaw is experimenting with AI-powered deliberation and town-hall tools to scale public input.
aiDemocracyAngle: Deploys AI-based tools like prebunking, DDoS protection for newsrooms, and deliberation platforms to defend elections and civic discourse from manipulation.

name: Kieskompas
tagline: 2D political-map VAA by André Krouwel, used in 40+ countries
description: Kieskompas (Election Compass) is a Dutch voting advice application founded in 2006 by political scientist André Krouwel of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Unlike three-point statement tools, it places voters and parties on a two-dimensional political map derived from academic research on party positioning, with party stances determined by expert analysis of manifestos and public statements rather than party self-placement alone. Through its commercial arm, Kieskompas has built Election Compass projects used by millions of voters in more than 40 countries, and its large opt-in datasets feed academic research on party choice and voter behaviour. It is a classic, research-driven questionnaire VAA rather than an AI/LLM tool, distinguished by its spatial visualisation and expert-coded party positions.
aiDemocracyAngle: A research-grounded classic VAA whose global, expert-coded datasets are a key academic reference point for how voters and parties are matched.

name: Knight Foundation
tagline: ~$50M research field on how technology and AI reshape democracy
description: The John S. and James L. Knight Foundation, endowed by the Knight newspaper fortune, is a leading US funder of journalism and democracy that has built a major Technology and Democracy portfolio. It committed nearly $50M to develop a new field of research on how technology transforms democracy and how people receive and engage with information, funding centers at institutions including a $10M Center on Media, Technology, and Democracy at Penn and an Institute for Data, Democracy, and Politics at George Washington University. On AI specifically, Knight co-founded the 2017 Ethics and Governance of AI Fund (initial $27M, including $7.6M to nine civil-society organizations shaping AI in the public interest), and more recently committed $4M with USC Marshall to steer AI and social media toward human-centered outcomes, over $3M for city governments to use generative AI for civic engagement, and grants on AI, authorship, and copyright. Knight blends academic field-building with applied civic-tech and journalism support.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its Technology and Democracy program and AI ethics funds explicitly study and shape how AI and platforms affect democratic information ecosystems and civic life.
funders: Endowed by the fortune of newspaper publishers John S. and James L. Knight

name: Longview Philanthropy
tagline: Advises major donors on AI risk, including extreme power concentration
description: Longview Philanthropy is a UK/US grantmaking advisor that designs and runs funds for major donors on global catastrophic risks, with artificial intelligence as its largest focus. Its Emerging Challenges Fund backs work on AI, biosecurity, and nuclear risk. Most relevant here, Longview runs a dedicated Request for Proposals on Extreme Power Concentration, funding research and interventions to reduce the risk that advanced AI lets a small group seize durable control over everyone else, whether through AI companies accumulating power or authoritarian states entrenching AI-enabled military and police forces. Its framing explicitly ties safe AI to distributing compute across allied democracies rather than concentrating it. Longview advises high-net-worth individuals and institutions, structuring grants across technical safety, governance, and civil-society work. It positions power concentration alongside loss-of-control as a core catastrophic risk, making it one of the few funders with an explicit AI-and-democracy/power program rather than treating democracy as a side effect.

name: Loomio
tagline: Worker-cooperative software for transparent collaborative group decisions
description: Loomio is an open-source collaborative decision-making platform built since 2011 by a worker-owned cooperative in Aotearoa New Zealand, with roots in the Occupy movement. It gives groups a dedicated space, separate from email and chat, to discuss proposals, vote with reasoning, and build a searchable record of why each decision was made, supporting divergent exploration and convergent agreement. Loomio accommodates multiple governance models (consensus, consent, majority vote, advice process) and provides audit trails, recorded outcomes, quorum requirements, delegated voters, and timestamped votes for legitimate, defensible decisions. It is used by thousands of groups worldwide, including nonprofits, city councils, political parties, cooperatives, and social movements. As mature, self-governing decision infrastructure, Loomio is a key tool in the participatory-governance ecosystem; while not AI-centric, it exemplifies structured collective decision-making that adjacent AI-facilitation and summarization efforts aim to augment.
aiDemocracyAngle: Loomio operationalizes structured collective decision-making with full audit trails, providing a governance substrate that AI-facilitation research seeks to enhance.

name: Luminate
tagline: Omidyar's global fund for digital justice and equitable technology
description: Luminate is a global philanthropic organization founded by Pierre and Pam Omidyar, spun out of Omidyar Network's Governance and Citizen Engagement initiative in 2018. Today it frames its mission as advancing digital justice and equitable technology, having deployed over $370M to 500+ partners since 2018 through grants and impact investments in organizations that hold power to account and give people control over the information and systems shaping their lives. Its data-and-digital-rights work directly addresses how AI, platforms, and data concentration affect democratic participation, funding advocacy, research, and civil-society organizations across Europe, Africa, Latin America, the US, and Asia. Luminate incubated Reset Tech inside its London headquarters until 2024 and supports a broad ecosystem of digital-rights and accountability groups. While its mandate is democracy and open society broadly rather than AI specifically, its digital-rights portfolio increasingly targets algorithmic accountability, disinformation, and the governance of AI-enabled platforms as threats to and opportunities for democratic life.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its data and digital rights portfolio funds algorithmic accountability, platform governance, and disinformation work at the intersection of AI and democratic participation.

name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
tagline: Foundational voice on irreversible loss of human control over ASI
description: The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI) is a Berkeley-based nonprofit, active since 2000, that helped found the field of AI alignment. Its current focus has shifted heavily toward public communication and policy advocacy: MIRI argues that the default outcome of building artificial superintelligence is human extinction or total loss of human control, and calls for a global moratorium on ASI development. Its 2025 book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' and related media aim to make loss-of-control risk legible to policymakers and the public. While MIRI centers extinction and loss of control rather than intra-human power concentration, its framing, that decisive capability could pass irreversibly out of human hands, is foundational to the broader disempowerment discourse. MIRI conducts technical, philosophical and policy work and communicates through books, a newsletter and documentary projects.
aiDemocracyAngle: Foundational voice on irreversible loss of human control over superintelligence, the extreme end of the disempowerment spectrum, now focused on moratorium advocacy.

name: Macroscopic Ventures
tagline: Swiss nonprofit deploying up to $100M for AI safety and governance
description: Macroscopic Ventures is a Swiss nonprofit founded in 2019 in Basel that makes grants to nonprofits and investments in socially beneficial companies focused on reducing catastrophic AI risk. It aims to deploy up to $100M across AI (governance, policy, welfare, and cooperative AI), its 'Reason & Democracy' focus area (strengthening democratic institutions, rule of law and reducing authoritarianism risks), and animal welfare, and gave around $30M in grants in 2025. Its AI portfolio spans AI policy and governance, compute governance, information security, multi-agent and cooperative AI, and AI verification mechanisms. Past grantees include the NYU Mind, Ethics, and Policy Program, the Center on Long-Term Risk, the Institute for Law and AI, and the Cooperative AI Foundation, which it seeded with a $15M commitment; past investments include Anthropic's Series A and B. Its Reason & Democracy focus area, together with its governance and policy work, bears directly on preventing dangerous concentration of AI power.
aiDemocracyAngle: Funds AI governance, policy, cooperative AI, and work on malevolent actors and power that overlaps with preventing dangerous concentration of AI capability.
funders: Swiss nonprofit; deploys grants and impact investments (backers not fully public)

keyProjects.note: Governance, policy, cooperative AI, and security

keyProjects.note: AI, societal long-term risk, animal welfare

name: Make.org
tagline: European civic-tech platform running large AI-supported citizen consultations
description: Make.org is a European civic-tech organization that runs large-scale online citizen consultations ('Grandes Causes') and deliberative processes, gathering and synthesizing millions of citizen contributions on public issues. It applies natural-language processing and clustering to analyze massive volumes of open input, and built an AI tool called Panoramic that lets citizens, journalists, and civil-society organizations navigate the discussions and results of deliberative processes through an interactive interface. Make.org's platform supported analysis for France's Grand Débat National and the Citizens' Convention on the End of Life, using AI to summarize large information sets and increase transparency around deliberations. It has also coordinated an initiative bringing together CNRS, Sorbonne University, and Sciences Po to address the democratic risks of generative AI while harnessing it to strengthen participation. Make.org operates across multiple European countries as a mission-driven company.
aiDemocracyAngle: Make.org uses NLP and generative-AI tools like Panoramic to make million-scale citizen consultations tractable and transparent for both organizers and the public.

name: Meaning Alignment Institute
tagline: Aligning AI, markets and democracies with what people truly value
description: The Meaning Alignment Institute (MAI) is a nonprofit research organization (co-founded by Joe Edelman and Oliver Klingefjord, prominent from 2023) that studies how to align AI, markets and democracies with human values. It received an OpenAI Democratic Inputs to AI grant to build a novel democratic input mechanism for shaping how AI assistants behave. Its core method, Democratic Fine-Tuning (DFT), elicits people's deeper values and sources of meaning rather than surface preferences, then aggregates them into a moral graph used to steer model behavior, an alternative to standard RLHF or constitutional approaches. In work with OpenAI it produced a first moral graph showing that people across ideological divides often share underlying values. MAI's broader Full-Stack Alignment agenda seeks to align institutions, not just models, with what matters to people, drawing on ideas from Amartya Sen, Charles Taylor and Ruth Chang.
aiDemocracyAngle: Creates democratic, values-based methods for the public to shape AI behavior, finding common ground across ideological lines.

keyProjects.name: Democratic Fine-Tuning
keyProjects.note: Values-based method to steer LLM behavior

name: Metagov
tagline: Nonprofit collective building standards and infrastructure for digital self-governance
description: Metagov is a nonprofit research collective building standards and infrastructure for digital self-governance: a governance layer for the internet. Organized around three pillars (Community, Research, Operations), it convenes researchers and practitioners to study and prototype how online communities, platforms, and decentralized organizations govern themselves. Its projects include Govbase, a crowdsourced database of online-governance tools and projects; DAOstar, a standards body publishing technical standards for decentralized autonomous organizations; and PolicyKit, CommunityRule, and Modular Politics, which help online communities author and enact their own governance rules and processes. Metagov runs seminars, governance experiments, and cross-organization collaborations, functioning as connective research infrastructure for the wider field of computational and self-governance. While AI is not its exclusive focus, Metagov increasingly centers AI: its flagship Public AI initiative advocates publicly accountable AI infrastructure, alongside work on AI and agent governance and tooling for collective decision-making in digital communities.
aiDemocracyAngle: Metagov builds the standards and tooling layer for online self-governance, increasingly relevant to how AI agents and communities coordinate and make collective decisions.

keyProjects.name: Public AI
keyProjects.note: Flagship initiative advocating public, accountable AI infrastructure

name: Microsoft Tech for Society (formerly Democracy Forward)
tagline: Microsoft's program to protect elections and journalism in the AI era
description: Democracy Forward is a corporate-responsibility program at Microsoft (evolved from its 2018 Defending Democracy Program, renamed in 2021) that works to safeguard democratic processes from digital and AI-enabled threats. It combines cyber-protection, threat intelligence, tools and policy engagement. Ahead of the 2024 global year of elections it offered campaigns and election authorities services such as Content Credentials (provenance watermarking via the C2PA standard) to authenticate media, AccountGuard cyber-protection, and a portal to report deepfakes of candidates. Its Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center publishes reports on how nation-state actors weaponize AI in elections, finding that subtly AI-enhanced content often has more impact than fully synthetic media. The program also helps newsrooms adopt AI responsibly through journalism partnerships. Led by Ginny Badanes, Democracy Forward is a major platform company's institutional effort on AI and election integrity.
aiDemocracyAngle: Provides election authorities, campaigns and journalists with provenance tools, cyber-defense and threat intelligence against AI-enabled interference.

name: MIT Center for Collective Intelligence
tagline: Studying how people and computers can be connected to think together
description: The MIT Center for Collective Intelligence (CCI), founded in 2006 and directed by Thomas Malone, investigates how people and computers can be connected so that collectively they act more intelligently than any individual, group, or computer has before. Malone's framework of 'superminds' (hierarchies, markets, democracies, and communities) argues that groups of people (increasingly augmented by machines) are responsible for most human achievement, and that new technologies can make these superminds smarter by connecting humans in richer ways. CCI's research spans collective decision-making, prediction, problem-solving, and, more recently, how large language models and generative AI can augment or participate in human group intelligence. As one of the earliest academic centers dedicated to collective intelligence, CCI supplies foundational theory and experiments that inform the broader AI-augmented deliberation and governance field, including work on combining human and machine reasoning.
aiDemocracyAngle: CCI's 'supermind' research directly frames human-plus-AI systems as the unit of collective intelligence, underpinning modern AI-augmented decision-making design.

keyProjects.name: Superminds
keyProjects.note: Malone's foundational book on people + computers thinking together

name: MIT Center for Constructive Communication
tagline: MIT Media Lab center building tech and methods for constructive dialogue
description: The MIT Center for Constructive Communication (CCC) is a Media Lab research center founded in 2021 and directed by Deb Roy, who stepped down as Media Lab Executive Director to focus on dialogue and communication technology. CCC studies how social systems and technology shape public discourse and builds AI-assisted tools to surface underheard voices and foster understanding across divides. It works through a cooperation agreement with the nonprofit Cortico, incorporating Local Voices Network conversation data and 'sensemaking' methods into many projects that blend human-led facilitation with AI analysis. Research spans natural language processing of recorded small-group conversations, network analysis of media ecosystems, and designing alternatives to engagement-driven social platforms. As an academic home for constructive-communication research, CCC generates the methods and models that its sister organization Cortico deploys with communities, journalists, and civic institutions.
aiDemocracyAngle: CCC develops AI 'sensemaking' that analyzes facilitated human conversations at scale, aiming to strengthen democratic listening rather than optimize for engagement.

name: More in Common
tagline: Research to counter polarization and rebuild democratic social cohesion
description: More in Common is an international research and think-tank organization, founded in 2017 and named after murdered UK MP Jo Cox's maiden speech, that works to understand and counter polarization and division across Western democracies. With teams in the US, UK, France, Germany, Poland, Spain, and Brazil, it combines large-scale public-opinion research (its audience-segmentation work has engaged tens of thousands of people) with practical efforts to rebuild social cohesion and democratic resilience. It studies not just what people think but why, using social psychology and behavioral science, and partners with organizations that can act on its findings at scale. While not an AI organization, its research on polarization, trust, and social cohesion is directly relevant to how AI-mediated media and communication systems affect democratic societies, and it participates in cross-sector efforts (such as the Council on Technology and Social Cohesion) linking technology design to social cohesion.
aiDemocracyAngle: More in Common supplies the polarization and social-cohesion evidence base that any AI-and-democracy effort needs, defining the divisions that AI systems can either widen or bridge.

name: Mozilla Foundation
tagline: AI & Democracy Awards plus ~$20M/yr for trustworthy AI
description: The Mozilla Foundation, the nonprofit behind Firefox, invests about $20M annually in philanthropy and advocacy for trustworthy AI, data justice, and internet health. In late 2025 it announced the AI & Democracy Awards (applications from early 2026), a $1M program addressing the challenges AI poses to democratic institutions, information ecosystems, and civic participation. Running over 24 months, it supports 10 projects led by researchers, technologists, advocates, and communities working to ensure AI strengthens rather than undermines democratic life: ten awardees receive $50,000 to test approaches, with two finalists advancing to an additional $250,000 to scale. Mozilla also runs an Incubator, Creative AI Futures grants, and a Responsible Computing Challenge expanding into responsible AI. Its Trustworthy AI program funds and convenes work on transparency, accountability, and open-source alternatives to concentrated AI platforms. Mozilla combines grantmaking with advocacy, research (including its widely cited internet-health and AI transparency reports), and open-source tooling, giving it reach across builders, policymakers, and civil society.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its 2025 AI & Democracy Awards directly fund builders of alternatives protecting democratic institutions and information ecosystems from AI harms.
funders: Funded largely by Mozilla Corporation (Firefox) revenue and philanthropic partners

keyProjects.name: AI & Democracy Awards
keyProjects.note: $1M for 10 projects ensuring AI strengthens democracy

name: mySociety
tagline: Digital tools for democracy, transparency, and civic-tech evidence (TICTeC)
description: mySociety is a UK charity, founded in 2003, that builds digital tools to strengthen democracy, transparency, and community. Its long-running platforms include TheyWorkForYou (tracking MPs' votes and speeches), WhatDoTheyKnow (filing and publishing freedom-of-information requests), WriteToThem (contacting elected representatives), and FixMyStreet (reporting local problems). Its work spans four areas (transparency, democracy, community, and climate), and its commercial subsidiary SocietyWorks sells related services to local government to fund the charity. mySociety also convenes TICTeC (The Impacts of Civic Technology), the leading international conference and research community studying whether and how civic technology actually works, and it publishes research on digital democracy. As both a builder of widely used democratic infrastructure and a hub for evidence on civic-tech impact, mySociety is a foundational organization in the democratic-technology field and a natural reference point for anyone deploying AI to improve civic engagement.
aiDemocracyAngle: mySociety builds the mass-market civic infrastructure (parliamentary monitoring, FOI, representative contact) and, via TICTeC, curates the evidence base on what civic technology, now including AI, actually delivers for democracy.

name: National Democratic Institute (NDI)
tagline: Democracy-support group whose Democracy and Technology team defends information integrity worldwide
description: NDI (founded 1983, affiliated with the US Democratic Party but nonpartisan in mission) supports democratic institutions and processes in more than 100 countries. Its technology workstream is the Democracy and Technology team (DemTech), whose INFO/tegrity initiative leads NDI's work countering disinformation, hate speech, and online manipulation while strengthening information integrity. INFO/tegrity conducts research on disinformation vulnerability and resilience, monitors computational propaganda in elections, helps platforms 'design for democracy,' and has built regional civic-tech networks across Asia, Africa, Eurasia, and Latin America. NDI has published a primer on generative AI and electoral integrity, addressing how widely available gen-AI tools complicate efforts to protect elections.
aiDemocracyAngle: NDI's INFO/tegrity initiative counters AI-amplified disinformation and computational propaganda in elections, and pushes platforms to 'design for democracy' against generative-AI threats.

name: Nesta Centre for Collective Intelligence Design
tagline: UK innovation lab combining human and machine intelligence for social good
description: The Centre for Collective Intelligence Design (CCID) is a research and experimentation unit within Nesta, the UK innovation foundation. It is built on the premise that human collective intelligence combined with machine intelligence outperforms either alone, and it explores how to mobilize the two together at scale to address social challenges. CCID runs practical experiments and deliberative engagements, publishes a Collective Intelligence Design Playbook, and has operated grant programmes funding experiments (up to £30,000 each) in areas from climate action to crisis response. Its Collective Crisis Intelligence work fuses frontline community input with AI for faster, more effective disaster mitigation and recovery. The centre aims to break down barriers to participation, reimagine civic engagement, and rebuild trust between people and institutions using technology, AI, arts, and design. It functions as a European anchor for the collective-intelligence-design methodology.
aiDemocracyAngle: CCID explicitly designs systems that pair citizen participation with machine intelligence, treating human-AI collective intelligence as a tool for public problem-solving.

keyProjects.name: Collective Crisis Intelligence
keyProjects.note: Community input + AI for crisis response

name: New America — Political Reform
tagline: Evidence-based strategies to modernize and de-polarize US democracy
description: New America's Political Reform program develops evidence-based strategies to repair government dysfunction, rebuild civic trust, and modernize American democracy. Based in Washington, DC and led by Mark Schmitt with senior fellows including Lee Drutman and Hollie Russon Gilman, it studies electoral reform (challenging what Drutman calls the 'two-party doom loop'), co-governance and participatory policymaking, and how citizens engage in democracy beyond voting. The program publishes books, analyses, and practical tools and partners with policymakers, community organizations, and funders to implement reforms, operating under New America's broader 'Democratic Futures' agenda. While not primarily an AI organization, its work on participatory institutions, deliberation, and democratic reform provides the institutional-design frame into which AI-enabled participation tools must fit. It is an influential think-tank voice on structural democratic reform in the United States.
aiDemocracyAngle: Political Reform supplies the institutional-design agenda (electoral reform, co-governance, deliberation) that determines whether AI-enabled participation tools land in reformed, resilient democratic institutions.

name: newDemocracy Foundation
tagline: Australia's independent institute proving citizens can decide complex issues
description: The newDemocracy Foundation is Australia's leading independent, non-partisan research institute dedicated to strengthening democracy between elections, active for roughly two decades. It designs and runs real-world citizens' assemblies and citizens' juries: deliberative processes that convene randomly selected, representative groups of everyday people, give them balanced information and expert evidence, and support them to reach considered recommendations for decision-makers. The Foundation has delivered projects on issues from nuclear waste storage to housing and local governance, and publishes an extensive library of research and R&D notes on what works in deliberative practice, aiming to make these methods a normal part of governance rather than an experimental curiosity. A current priority is delivering a national pilot citizens' assembly and building toward permanent national deliberative capability. Its focus is deliberative-democracy method and evidence rather than AI, but it is a foundational research anchor for the global field.
aiDemocracyAngle: As a rigorous method-and-evidence anchor for deliberation, newDemocracy shapes the standards that AI-assisted assembly tools are measured against.

name: Odyssean Institute
tagline: UK charity combining computational foresight with participatory deliberation
description: The Odyssean Institute is a UK-registered charity (no. 1204794) that blends computational foresight methods with participatory deliberation to improve how societies navigate global risks. Its flagship methodology, the Odyssean Process, combines expert elicitation, horizon scanning and deliberative mini-publics into a structured approach to policymaking under deep uncertainty. Current workstreams include an AI Governance Assembly applying the process to AI policy, GRAIN (research on global catastrophic risks) and a Resilient Supply Chains project. Key people: Giuseppe Dal Prá.
aiDemocracyAngle: Applies its Odyssean Process to AI governance, using deliberative mini-publics and foresight methods so AI policy is shaped by structured public deliberation.

name: OECD Innovative Citizen Participation Network
tagline: Global network institutionalizing deliberative democracy and citizens' assemblies
description: The OECD's Innovative Citizen Participation (ICP) Network, launched in 2019 within the OECD's Open Government work, is an international network of policymakers, organizers, academics, and designers advancing deliberative democracy (citizens' assemblies, juries, and panels) for public decision-making. Its landmark 2020 report, 'Innovative Citizen Participation and New Democratic Institutions: Catching the Deliberative Wave,' analyzed 289 case studies (1986-2019), identified twelve models of deliberative processes, defined good-practice principles, and mapped routes to institutionalizing citizen deliberation. The Network continues to publish guidance (including 'Eight Ways to Institutionalise Deliberative Democracy') and to support governments convening representative deliberative processes on issues from climate to infrastructure. As an intergovernmental effort, it lends official legitimacy and comparative evidence to deliberative democracy worldwide, providing the institutional templates that AI-assisted deliberation and sortition tools increasingly aim to support and scale.
aiDemocracyAngle: The OECD ICP Network sets the global standard for deliberative democratic institutions, the citizens'-assembly formats that AI deliberation and sortition tools are being built to support and scale.

name: Omidyar Network
tagline: $30M+ for responsible AI and guardrails serving democracy
description: Omidyar Network, the philanthropic investment firm created by eBay founder Pierre Omidyar, funds work to reshape technology, markets, and governance toward a more equitable society, with responsible technology and AI a central focus. It launched a dedicated effort to promote inclusive and responsible development of generative AI, committing an initial $30M across a slate of organizations, and helped anchor a Ford Foundation-led multi-funder initiative contributing more than $200M toward public-interest efforts to mitigate AI harms and promote responsible innovation. Its Responsible Technology portfolio has funded groups including the Center for Digital Democracy, Public Citizen, Color of Change, and Fight for the Future, plus a Tech Journalism Fund for in-depth AI reporting. Omidyar Network also incubated organizations that spun out as independent funders, including Luminate (its governance and citizen-engagement arm) and Reset Tech. It pairs grants with impact investments and policy advocacy, positioning itself against Big Tech's concentrated power over democratic discourse.
aiDemocracyAngle: Runs a dedicated responsible-AI funding effort and anchors the $200M cross-funder push to build ethical guardrails protecting the public interest and democratic discourse from AI harms.
funders: Pierre Omidyar (eBay founder) and Pam Omidyar

name: OpenVAA
tagline: Open-source framework to build VAAs anywhere, funded by Sitra
description: OpenVAA is an open-source framework for building voting advice applications, developed by OpenVAA ry, a non-profit association in Finland, with a developer release originally targeted for 2025. Its goal is to give any organisation a transparent, free, fully localisable and modular platform to run a VAA in any electoral context, lowering the barrier for new and under-resourced democracies. The project is funded by Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund, and is paired with a research strand, YouthVAA at the University of Helsinki, studying how VAAs are used and building a tool aimed at young, first-time voters. The code is on GitHub. OpenVAA itself is classic questionnaire-VAA infrastructure, but its openness makes it a natural substrate for experimenting with AI-enhanced features.
aiDemocracyAngle: Open, modular VAA infrastructure that could become the base layer for many tools, including AI-augmented voting advice.

name: Oxford Internet Institute — Programme on Democracy & Technology
tagline: Oxford's DemTech, pioneers of 'computational propaganda' research
description: The Programme on Democracy & Technology (DemTech) at the University of Oxford's Internet Institute, previously known as the Computational Propaganda Project (ComProp), has since 2012 investigated the use of algorithms, automation, and computational propaganda in public life. It coined the term 'computational propaganda' and produced the influential Global Inventory of Organised Social Media Manipulation (final edition 2021, covering 81 countries), which documented organized manipulation campaigns operating in 81 countries. Its case studies analyze cyber troops, state-sponsored media, bot networks, and foreign influence operations across dozens of elections and crises, combining computational, quantitative, and qualitative evidence. The programme's work is a foundational academic reference for understanding how automation and AI shape political communication.
aiDemocracyAngle: DemTech pioneered the study of computational propaganda (algorithmically amplified, increasingly AI-generated political manipulation) and maps its industrial-scale spread across the world's democracies.

keyProjects.note: Annual report on state-linked manipulation in 80+ countries

name: Partnership on AI (PAI)
tagline: Multistakeholder standards for responsible AI and synthetic media
description: Partnership on AI (PAI) is a nonprofit founded in 2016 by major AI labs, tech companies and civil-society groups to develop responsible-AI practices; it now convenes more than 100 partner organizations across industry, academia and civil society. Its most democracy-relevant work is the Responsible Practices for Synthetic Media Framework (launched February 2023), a voluntary standard for how to create, distribute and build technology for AI-generated media, covering consent, disclosure and labeling. With more than 70 elections in 2024, PAI convened a Community of Practice on AI and elections, applied its framework to real deepfake cases in Slovakia, Pakistan and the US, and published case studies (with BBC, OpenAI, TikTok and others) plus a glossary for synthetic-media transparency methods. PAI translates high-level principles into concrete, testable practices that platforms and creators can adopt to protect the information environment.
aiDemocracyAngle: Sets multistakeholder norms for labeling and disclosing synthetic media so AI-generated content doesn't erode election integrity and public trust.

keyProjects.name: AI and Elections Community of Practice

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
tagline: ~$500M for AI in the public interest and community power over AI
description: The Patrick J. McGovern Foundation (PJMF), endowed by the estate of IDG founder Patrick J. McGovern, is among the largest funders of public-purpose AI globally, having made roughly $500M in grants over the past decade. In December 2025 it announced a $75.8M commitment across 149 grants in 13 countries, supporting AI for human rights, media and journalism, climate resilience, crisis response, digital literacy, and health equity. Its stated philosophy is explicitly democratic: when people decide how AI is applied to real needs, technology can strengthen democracy, protect human rights, and widen opportunity. Its grants aim to build civic infrastructure that gives communities power over the systems affecting their lives. Examples include newsrooms using AI to review public documents and hold power to account, and a $500,000 grant to Georgetown's CSET supporting diversity and democracy in cybersecurity policy. PJMF pairs grantmaking with in-house data and AI capacity-building for nonprofits and public institutions.
aiDemocracyAngle: Frames its entire grantmaking around building civic infrastructure and community power over AI so the technology strengthens democracy and human rights.
funders: Endowed by the estate of Patrick J. McGovern, founder of IDG

name: People Powered — Global Hub for Participatory Democracy
tagline: Global member network growing participatory democracy programs
description: People Powered is a global hub for participatory democracy: the direct involvement of community members in policy decisions affecting their lives. Founded in 2020 and led by Executive Director Greta Rios, it operates as a member-driven organization uniting governments, practitioners, researchers, and advocates to grow their collective impact. People Powered synthesizes global knowledge into practical toolkits and connects governments and organizations with mentorship, training, and accelerator programs to launch and improve participatory budgeting, citizens' assemblies, and other participation programs. Its staff and members span the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia. People Powered runs programming on digital participation and the responsible use of AI in democratic processes, including guidance and case studies (such as vTaiwan's hybrid AI-assisted approach), and builds capacity across the worldwide participatory-democracy field, bridging grassroots practice and institutional adoption.
aiDemocracyAngle: People Powered runs dedicated programs on digital participation and responsible AI in democracy, helping practitioners adopt AI-assisted deliberation tools safely.

keyProjects.note: Guidance and case studies incl. AI-assisted deliberation

name: Perplexity Election Information Hub
tagline: Perplexity's source-grounded AI election hub for the 2024 US vote
description: The Election Information Hub was a dedicated feature launched by AI search company Perplexity for the 2024 US elections, offering AI-summarized, real-time voter guidance. Users could ask about voting requirements, polling places and hours, and get summaries of ballot measures, candidates and their stated positions and endorsements, at state and national level. Perplexity grounded the hub in vetted, nonpartisan sources (election data from Democracy Works and the Associated Press, plus references like Ballotpedia) to reduce the misinformation risks documented in AI-chatbot studies, and made it free without a subscription. Praised by outlets including Forbes and TechCrunch for accuracy and design, it is a leading example of a major AI company building a purpose-grounded election product rather than relying on a raw chatbot.
aiDemocracyAngle: A high-profile case of an LLM company shipping a source-grounded election product: the industry's answer to the AI voter-misinformation problem.

name: Plurality Institute
tagline: Hub for the plurality research community: tech for cooperation across difference
description: The Plurality Institute is a research hub organizing the emerging 'plurality' field: the study of technology that enables human cooperation at scale across social difference. It convenes academics in computer science, political science, and philosophy alongside industry and government researchers, spanning AI to peace studies. The Institute is closely tied to the book Plurality: The Future of Collaborative Technology and Democracy by E. Glen Weyl, Audrey Tang, and the Plurality community, whose steering committee overlaps with the Institute. Its work emphasizes using large language models and computational tools to improve public discourse and deliberative decision-making. Projects include BridgingBot (an LLM-powered social media moderator built with Harvard, UC Berkeley, Jigsaw, and Google.org), an LLM Map cataloguing 70+ tools that use language models to strengthen public discourse, OpenBallot for comparing voter guidance, and R&D micro-grants to accelerate 'plural' technology development.
aiDemocracyAngle: The Institute explicitly maps and funds LLM-based tools for bridging divides and healthier discourse, positioning AI as connective tissue for pluralistic democracy.

keyProjects.note: Weyl/Tang open-source book anchoring the field

keyProjects.note: Compare ballot recommendations from trusted sources

name: POPVOX Foundation
tagline: Helping Congress and legislatures adopt AI and modernize responsibly
description: The POPVOX Foundation is a nonprofit (the 501(c)(3) sibling of the civic-tech company POPVOX) dedicated to helping democratic institutions, especially the U.S. Congress and other legislatures, keep pace with a rapidly changing world. It works across governing capacity and technology, legislative strengthening, and constituent engagement, offering technical assistance, research, and prototyping. Its AI work centers on 'AI Base Camp,' hands-on guidance for congressional staff on prompting, coding, autonomous agents, and chamber-specific applications, plus resources on AI policy risks like vendor lock-in. Other initiatives include the Digital Parliaments Project, Future-Proofing Congress, Modern Parliament, casework resources, the Departure Dialogues project, and the Gavel In podcast. POPVOX Foundation is one of the few organizations working directly inside legislative institutions on responsible adoption of AI and emerging technology, making it a bridge between AI capability and democratic capacity.
aiDemocracyAngle: POPVOX Foundation is a rare org embedding AI directly into legislative practice, training Congress on AI and modernizing parliaments, so democratic institutions can actually use the technology responsibly.

name: Power for Democracies
tagline: Berlin hub steering donors to effective democracy-defense giving
description: Power for Democracies is a Berlin-based nonprofit founded in 2023 by Markus N. Beeko (former secretary general of Amnesty International Germany) with philanthropy-advisory founders Stefan Shaw and Stephan Schwahlen. Its mission is to advance and protect liberal democracy worldwide by recommending highly effective civil-society initiatives for donors to support. It first took shape as a fund within Effektiv Spenden (Germany's effective-giving organization) before becoming independent, and works closely with small family foundations and private individuals in Germany and Switzerland to channel funding to effective pro-democracy work. Rather than running a single program, it synthesizes existing research, commissions original studies where gaps exist, and produces actionable donor recommendations and methodologies for civil society, with a team of political scientists, mathematicians, sociologists, and practitioners across Berlin, Nairobi, Washington, Oxford, and Bogota. As democracies confront AI-enabled disinformation and manipulation, its evidence-led donor guidance increasingly shapes where funding for democratic resilience, including against digital and AI threats, is directed.
aiDemocracyAngle: An evidence-led democracy-philanthropy hub that steers donor funding toward the most effective defenses of liberal democracy, increasingly including AI-enabled digital threats.
funders: Small family foundations and private donors in Germany and Switzerland; incubated within Effektiv Spenden

name: Protect Democracy — AI for Democracy Action Lab
tagline: Nonpartisan action tank defending democracy in the AI era
description: The AI for Democracy Action Lab (AI-DAL) is a multidisciplinary, nonpartisan action tank at Protect Democracy, a US nonprofit founded in 2017 to prevent American democracy from declining into a more authoritarian form of government. AI-DAL brings together technologists, lawyers, policy experts and engineers to both defend against AI's dangers to democracy and harness AI to strengthen self-government. It works along two tracks: incubating and accelerating AI-enabled civic tools by partnering with organizations pioneering pro-democracy applications, and developing policy and governance solutions that check AI-enhanced threats. It advises platforms and regulators on embedding constitutional principles like checks-and-balances, individual freedoms and privacy in tech governance. Recent work includes defending frontier AI labs' safety guardrails against government overreach in court and Congress. AI-DAL pairs concrete tool-building with legal and policy advocacy.
aiDemocracyAngle: Both builds pro-democracy AI tools and shapes law/policy to blunt AI-enabled authoritarian threats, grounded in constitutional principles.
