name: RadicalxChange
tagline: Movement advancing new mechanisms for democracy, markets, and data
description: RadicalxChange (RxC) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and global movement founded in 2018, associated with economist E. Glen Weyl, dedicated to reimagining the institutions of democracy, markets, property, and data for a more equitable and cooperative society. It develops and experiments with 'radical social technologies': quadratic voting and quadratic funding (for expressing preference intensity and funding public goods), data sovereignty and data coalitions, and new approaches to property and privacy-preserving collective decision-making. RxC builds community through local chapters, conferences, education, and open-source experiments, and its ideas have influenced blockchain governance, participatory budgeting, and plurality thinking (Weyl co-authored the Plurality book). While rooted in mechanism design and political economy rather than AI specifically, RxC's tools for aggregating preferences and funding public goods are foundational infrastructure for technology-augmented collective decision-making and increasingly inform AI-governance and digital-democracy design.
aiDemocracyAngle: RxC's mechanisms like quadratic voting and funding are core primitives for tech-mediated collective choice, increasingly applied to AI governance and public-goods funding.

name: Remesh
tagline: AI platform for real-time back-and-forth conversation with large live audiences
description: Remesh is an AI-powered insights platform that enables a facilitator to hold a structured, back-and-forth conversation with a live audience of hundreds of participants simultaneously. Participants answer open-ended questions in their own words and also vote on and rank each other's responses; Remesh's algorithms analyze responses in real time, predict how the whole group would vote on each statement, and surface where consensus and division lie. This lets organizers understand a large group's views at speed and pivot the conversation as insights emerge. While Remesh is a commercial market-research and employee-insights product, its consensus-surfacing dialogue mechanism has been used for civic and deliberative applications, including large public and stakeholder consultations. It represents the applied, enterprise-grade end of AI-augmented opinion aggregation, closely related in method to Pol.is-style consensus discovery.
aiDemocracyAngle: Remesh's AI engine aggregates and ranks open-ended input from hundreds of live participants, offering scalable real-time consensus-finding usable for civic deliberation.

keyProjects.name: Remesh platform
keyProjects.note: AI dialogue platform for hundreds of live participants

name: Reset Tech
tagline: Grants and advocacy to protect democracy from digital threats
description: Reset Tech is a public-policy organization launched in 2019 to protect democracy from digital threats and hold Big Tech accountable, combining research, policy analysis, advocacy, and grantmaking to ensure technologies are safe and secure for children, consumers, and public safety. It provides grants and contracts to partners pursuing a shared policy, technology, and advocacy agenda in countries with immediate opportunities for change, with strong activity in Europe around platform regulation and digital threats to elections and public discourse. Reset Tech was incubated inside Luminate's London headquarters (until January 2024) and is backed by a coalition of philanthropies including Luminate, the Ford Foundation (core support), Omidyar Network, the Children's Investment Fund Foundation, the Skoll Foundation, and the Alfred Landecker Foundation for its European work. As generative AI intensifies disinformation and manipulation risks, Reset Tech's regranting and advocacy increasingly target the algorithmic and AI dimensions of threats to democratic information ecosystems.
aiDemocracyAngle: A regranting advocacy organization explicitly built to protect democracy from digital and increasingly AI-driven threats to information ecosystems and elections.

name: Rethink Priorities
tagline: Cross-cause research nonprofit; its AI governance team spun out as IAPS
description: Rethink Priorities is a research nonprofit (founded 2018, US-based/remote) that conducts cross-cause prioritization research, formerly including a dedicated AI Governance and Strategy team, which has since spun out as the independent Institute for AI Policy and Strategy (IAPS, iaps.ai). Its AI work analyzed how to steer the development and deployment of transformative AI, and touches directly on power concentration, for example examining how very powerful AI could concentrate returns and control in a few corporate or state hands, and evaluating models of public AI development, ownership and democratic oversight as counterweights. Rethink Priorities produces empirical and strategic reports, survey work, and talent pipelines (including contractor and fellowship pools) feeding the broader AI-governance field. While power concentration is one strand within a wider portfolio spanning global health, animal welfare and existential risk, that governance analysis now continues at IAPS.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its former AI governance team (now the independent IAPS) studied how AI could concentrate economic and political control and weighed public-ownership and oversight models as democratic counterweights.

name: Schmidt Sciences (AI2050)
tagline: Eric & Wendy Schmidt fellowships for societally beneficial AI
description: AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative of Schmidt Sciences, funded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt and co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, supporting exceptional researchers working on the hard problems and opportunities critical to get right for society to benefit from AI. It awards AI2050 Fellowships of $300,000-$500,000 over three years to early-career and senior fellows; its 2025 cohort made 28 scholars eligible for more than $18M, bringing the program to 99 fellows across eight countries and 42 institutions. The framing, motivated by the question of what the world should do to realize AI's benefits and avoid its pitfalls by 2050, spans trustworthy and safe models, AI for science, and the societal and governance dimensions of AI. Schmidt Sciences (formerly part of Schmidt Futures) is a broad science philanthropy; AI2050 is its flagship AI vehicle. While not a democracy-specific program, its safety, trust, and societal-impact strands intersect with keeping AI accountable to the public.
aiDemocracyAngle: Funds research on making AI trustworthy, safe, and beneficial to society, including governance and societal-impact questions that bear on democratic accountability of AI.
funders: Eric and Wendy Schmidt (via Schmidt Sciences)

name: Siegel Family Endowment
tagline: David Siegel's foundation on technology's impact on society
description: The Siegel Family Endowment, founded in 2011 by Two Sigma co-founder David Siegel, is a New York foundation dedicated to understanding and shaping the impact of technology on society. It uses an inquiry-driven grantmaking approach across three interest areas at the intersection of learning, workforce, and infrastructure, awarding large annual portfolios (recent rounds have exceeded $15-16M). Its AI-related grants focus heavily on the workforce and public-interest technology dimensions of AI, supporting worker-informed research and pilots that center worker voice in the design and deployment of AI, reduce information asymmetries, and generate evidence to influence employers, policymakers, and the broader field. It also funds public-interest technology infrastructure and community-centered innovation around AI. While the endowment is not framed as a democracy funder, its emphasis on ensuring AI and emerging technologies serve workers, communities, and public institutions rather than concentrating advantage connects to broader questions of technology's compatibility with an equitable, participatory society.
aiDemocracyAngle: Funds worker- and community-centered research on AI deployment and public-interest technology infrastructure, keeping AI accountable to the people it affects.

name: Simon Institute for Longterm Governance
tagline: Geneva think tank for international cooperation on transformative AI
description: The Simon Institute for Longterm Governance (SI) is a Geneva-based think tank focused on international cooperation for governing transformative technologies, especially frontier AI. Working at the interface of the multilateral system (including UN processes), SI conducts research on global AI governance, facilitates dialogue between technical experts and diplomats, and trains civil servants on AI's risks and governance. Its relevance to power concentration is twofold: it studies how to build cooperative institutions that prevent destabilizing races and unilateral control over transformative AI, and it has convened work on benefit-sharing, for example the Windfall Trust workshop on redistributing AI profits rather than letting them concentrate. By strengthening international coordination and the capacity of governments to steer AI, SI aims to keep decisions about transformative technology accountable and broadly distributed rather than captured by a few actors.
aiDemocracyAngle: Builds the international-cooperation and benefit-sharing institutions meant to stop transformative AI from concentrating power in a few states or firms.

name: smartvote
tagline: Switzerland's VAA with candidate-level matching and smartspider visuals
description: smartvote is Switzerland's leading voting advice application, operated since 2004 by the politically neutral non-profit association Politools. Voters complete a long questionnaire of 30-75 policy questions and are matched not only with parties but with individual candidates, who answer the same questionnaire themselves. Results are shown through distinctive visualisations, the 'smartspider' and 'smartmap.' Since 2003 it has served voters in over 350 elections in Switzerland and, through smartvote International, has been adapted for elections abroad, including Australia. It is regarded as one of the most methodologically detailed VAAs because of its unusually long questionnaire and candidate-level matching. smartvote is a classic questionnaire-based tool rather than an AI system, valued for neutrality and transparency.
aiDemocracyAngle: A gold-standard classic VAA notable for candidate-level matching and rich visual analytics, widely cited in VAA research.

name: Sortition Foundation
tagline: Recruits representative citizens' panels by democratic lottery
description: The Sortition Foundation is a nonprofit that campaigns for a world where representative, randomly selected samples of everyday people make decisions in informed, deliberative citizens' assemblies. In practice it provides the sortition (democratic lottery) services that underpin assemblies: mailing invitations to households selected at random from address databases, then using an open-source stratification algorithm to select a broadly representative panel across age, gender, geography, socioeconomic proxy, and relevant attitudes. The Foundation's selection software and 'fairest-possible' algorithm have been used to recruit dozens of panels, including for Climate Assembly UK. Beyond service delivery it advocates for embedding sortition into governance as a permanent feature of democracy. While the Foundation's core is logistics and campaigning rather than AI, its algorithmic selection work sits at the intersection of fairness, computation, and democratic legitimacy, and it is a key operational partner for assemblies run by other organizations in this ecosystem.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its open-source fair-selection algorithms bring computational fairness to who gets a seat at deliberation, a quiet but load-bearing piece of tech-enabled democracy.

name: Stanford Deliberative Democracy Lab
tagline: Home of Deliberative Polling and an AI-assisted online deliberation platform
description: The Deliberative Democracy Lab (formerly the Center for Deliberative Democracy) at Stanford University is directed by James Fishkin, originator of the Deliberative Polling method. Deliberative Polling brings together a randomly selected, representative sample of people for informed, balanced discussion of policy issues, measuring how considered opinion shifts; the method has been applied in more than 150 experiments across over 50 countries. The lab, with Stanford's Crowdsourced Democracy Team, developed an Online Deliberation Platform featuring an AI-assisted virtual moderator that offers discussion prompts, encourages quieter participants, curbs abusive speech, and manages the agenda, enabling structured small-group deliberation at scale without human facilitators for every group. The platform has powered online Deliberative Polls internationally. The lab combines rigorous social-science measurement of deliberation with automation that lowers the cost of running high-quality deliberative processes.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its Online Deliberation Platform embeds an AI virtual moderator to automate facilitation, making representative deliberation scalable while preserving quality.

name: StemWijzer / VoteMatch
tagline: The Netherlands' original 1989 VAA, most-used in the country, by ProDemos
description: StemWijzer (internationally VoteMatch) is the Netherlands' most-used voting advice application, developed by ProDemos, the Dutch 'House for Democracy and the Rule of Law.' Originating in 1989 as the first such tool in the country (initially on paper and floppy disk) and online since 1998, it asks voters for their position on 30 statements on a three-point scale and returns a ranking of parties by alignment. In a recent Dutch general election it was completed around 3.2 million times in a month. It also runs for European Parliament, provincial and municipal elections. StemWijzer inspired a wave of European VAAs, including Germany's Wahl-O-Mat. It is a classic statement-based questionnaire, prized for simplicity and neutrality, not an AI tool.
aiDemocracyAngle: The historical progenitor of the modern VAA genre that later AI voting tools are explicitly measured against.

name: Stiftung Mercator
tagline: German foundation funding AI use aligned with democratic values
description: Stiftung Mercator is a major German private foundation, funded by the Schmidt-Ruthenbeck family's Metro retail fortune, whose Digital Society program aims to ensure digital technologies in Germany and Europe are developed and used in accordance with democratic rights and values. It funds projects on the increasing use of AI in areas relevant to the public, the regulation of digital platforms, the shift of public discourse to digital spaces, and state modernization. It established Agora Digitale Transformation, an independent digital-policy think tank, with roughly EUR 8.6M over an initial five years, and supports organizations such as AlgorithmWatch that scrutinize automated decision-making. In 2024 it approved 108 new projects worth over EUR 58M across Digital Society, Europe in the World, Climate, and Cohesion, and it co-funded (EUR 4M with partners) the Humboldt Institute for Internet and Society. Its AI work includes transatlantic exchange on aligning AI development with democratic principles.
aiDemocracyAngle: Its Digital Society program explicitly funds AI and platform work to keep technology aligned with democratic rights and values in Germany and Europe.
funders: Endowed by the Schmidt-Ruthenbeck family (Metro AG retail fortune)

keyProjects.name: Digital Society program
keyProjects.note: Funds AI and platform work aligned with democratic values

name: Survival and Flourishing Fund
tagline: Jaan Tallinn's fund: ~$152M to AI safety and resilient institutions
description: The Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF), founded by Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn, organizes the evaluation and distribution of donations to organizations concerned with the long-term survival and flourishing of sentient life. Initially seeded in 2019 via a ~$2M grant routed through the Berkeley Existential Risk Initiative from Tallinn's donations, SFF has since distributed roughly $152M, including $34.9M in 2025. It focuses heavily on AI safety and AI governance, alongside biosecurity and institutional resilience, using a distinctive S-Process evaluation method in which multiple independent recommenders allocate funds. It offers rolling Speculation Grants, an annual competitive S-Process round, and Initiative Committee funding, with individual grants ranging from $10,000 to $4,000,000. Its 2026 round is expected to distribute $20-40M across a main round and theme rounds. SFF is a central pipeline of funding to the AI-safety ecosystem, including many governance and institutional-resilience organizations whose work underpins democratic oversight of advanced AI.
aiDemocracyAngle: A major funder of AI governance and institutional-resilience organizations whose work supports democratic oversight and resilience against AI-driven catastrophic risk.
funders: Jaan Tallinn (Skype co-founder); Astera Foundation supports Speculation Grants

keyProjects.name: 2026 grant round
keyProjects.note: Est. $20-40M across main and theme rounds

name: TrueMedia.org
tagline: Free AI detector for political deepfakes in social media
description: TrueMedia.org is a nonpartisan, nonprofit tool that detects manipulated and AI-generated political media. Founded in 2024 and originally led by AI researcher Oren Etzioni (founding CEO of the Allen Institute for AI), it launched a free deepfake detector ahead of the 2024 US election that lets journalists, fact-checkers and the public submit links from platforms like X, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and Facebook and receive an authenticity assessment. The system aggregates results from multiple third-party detection models plus human review, reporting roughly 90% accuracy alongside transparency about its limitations, and it partnered with Microsoft's AI for Good Lab on detection. In 2025 the project moved to Georgetown University's McCourt School of Public Policy, where it continues as open, research-driven, non-proprietary infrastructure for information integrity rather than a closed commercial service.
aiDemocracyAngle: Gives newsrooms and voters a fast way to check whether viral political images, audio and video are AI fabrications.

keyProjects.name: TrueMedia Deepfake Detector
keyProjects.note: Detector in beta at Georgetown; access by request

name: V-Dem Institute (Varieties of Democracy)
tagline: World's largest democracy dataset, measuring digital disinformation across 180+ countries
description: Based at the University of Gothenburg, V-Dem produces the world's largest dataset on democracy, with hundreds of indicators rated by 4,000+ country experts. Its technology workstream is the Digital Society Project (DSP), a dedicated survey module co-directed with researchers that generates 35+ indicators across five areas: government disinformation, digital media freedom, state regulation of digital media, online media polarization, and online social cleavages. DSP provides novel measures estimating the volume of state-produced disinformation in ~148-180 countries since 2000, feeding V-Dem's annual Democracy Report on autocratization. Its 'Digital Repression in Autocracies' research documents how regimes weaponize online tools. This lets scholars empirically test how AI- and internet-enabled disinformation correlates with democratic backsliding.
aiDemocracyAngle: The Digital Society Project quantifies state-sponsored disinformation and digital repression worldwide, providing the empirical backbone for studying how AI-amplified information manipulation drives autocratization.

keyProjects.name: Digital Society Project
keyProjects.note: 35+ indicators on disinformation and digital media freedom

name: Vote Compass
tagline: Broadcaster-scale VAA (CBC/ABC) built by Vox Pop Labs for electoral literacy
description: Vote Compass is a civic-engagement application developed by Vox Pop Labs, a team of social and data scientists led by founder Clifton van der Linden. Distributed with major broadcasters, most prominently the CBC in Canada and the ABC in Australia, it asks users about 30 issues drawn from the campaign and shows how their views align with the competing parties, along with links to where parties actually stated each position. Questions are built with political scientists from public statements and party disclosures, then narrowed using public surveys of salient issues. Deliberately not a 'how to vote' tool, it emphasises electoral literacy over recommendation. Millions have used it across Canadian, Australian and other elections. It is a classic questionnaire-and-analytics VAA rather than an LLM system.
aiDemocracyAngle: A broadcaster-scale classic VAA emphasising electoral literacy and transparent sourcing rather than a direct vote recommendation.

name: VOTE411
tagline: League of Women Voters' nonpartisan personalized US voter guide
description: VOTE411 is the League of Women Voters' online voter guide, launched in 2006 by the LWV Education Fund. Voters enter their address to see their personalized ballot, candidates' own answers to League-provided questions, ballot measures, polling places, key dates and a first-time-voter checklist. Local Leagues gather candidate information across all 50 states and DC, and the guide is offered in English and Spanish and updated throughout the cycle. Strictly nonpartisan, it presents candidates' unedited responses side by side rather than recommending anyone. It has served tens of millions of voters, reached over three million people in 2023 alone, and won a Webby People's Voice Award and an Anthem Award. It is a classic voter-information guide, not an AI or questionnaire-matching tool.
aiDemocracyAngle: A trusted nonpartisan voter-information backbone in the US, the kind of authoritative source AI election tools cite for ballot and candidate data.

name: Voto Informado CR
tagline: Privacy-first VAA for Costa Rica's 2026 elections
description: Voto Informado CR is a Costa Rican voting advice platform for the 2026 general elections, built by the studio Maldron. It offers clear, neutral electoral information and a lightweight VAA: users answer a 19-question survey on key issues, see which parties align with their values, and browse detailed candidate and party proposals by topic across presidential and legislative races. A notable privacy feature is that responses are processed locally in the browser and never sent to a server. It reflects the spread of the VAA format into Latin America alongside similar efforts like Ecuador's Brújula Electoral. The tool relies on structured questionnaires and curated proposal data rather than AI, making it a classic, privacy-forward VAA for a newer VAA market.
aiDemocracyAngle: Evidence that the classic VAA model is spreading to Latin America with a privacy-first, local-only design: fertile ground for future AI features.

name: vTaiwan
tagline: Taiwan's pioneering Pol.is-powered online consultation-to-legislation process
description: vTaiwan is an open consultation process launched in 2015 that pairs online deliberation with in-person discussion to help the Taiwanese government develop consensus and recommendations on national legislation. Emerging from the 2014 Sunflower Movement and the g0v civic-tech community, it uses Pol.is to gather and cluster stakeholder opinions, giving visibility to statements that find consensus across ideological groups while suppressing purely divisive framing. Experts, officials, stakeholders, and citizens then work from that surfaced common ground toward policy. It became the world's most-cited example of government-scale digital deliberation: an early 2015 process on Uber regulation produced consensus statements that informed new rules, and by 2018 it had addressed 26 issues, most leading to decisive government action. Now largely volunteer-driven and serving as a civic laboratory, vTaiwan has also hosted experiments with AI-assisted analysis (including Talk to the City), making it a living testbed for AI-augmented democratic consultation.
aiDemocracyAngle: vTaiwan is the canonical proving ground where Pol.is consensus-mapping, and now LLM tools like Talk to the City, feeds directly into national policymaking.

name: wahl.chat
tagline: AI chat over German party manifestos and voting records
description: wahl.chat is an AI chatbot for German elections, created in early 2025 by a team from TUM, LMU and the University of Cambridge (Sebastian Maier, Anton Wyrowski, Michel Schimpf, Robin Frasch and Roman Mayr). Instead of fixed theses, it lets users hold an open dialogue about party positions for the 2025 Bundestag election, covering CDU/CSU, SPD, Greens, FDP, Die Linke, AfD, BSW and Volt. It is built on large language models such as GPT-4o combined with Perplexity-style retrieval, grounding answers in official party manifestos, records of actual Bundestag votes and news sources to gauge how realistic promises are. The codebase is open source and the project runs on donations. It has since been adapted for German state elections, including the 2026 Rhineland-Palatinate and Saxony-Anhalt votes, in cooperation with Open Parliament TV and Cambridge.
aiDemocracyAngle: A conversational, LLM-based successor to the Wahl-O-Mat that grounds open-ended answers in manifestos and voting records via RAG.

name: Wahl-O-Chat
tagline: Academic RAG chatbot citing German party manifestos, by FH Südwestfalen
description: Wahl-O-Chat is an AI chatbot built by Prof. Christian Gawron of Fachhochschule Südwestfalen (Iserlohn) for Germany's 2025 federal election, created as a teaching and research demonstrator for retrieval-augmented generation in the university's Applied AI programme. It uses the GPT-4o-mini language model grounded in the manifestos of AfD, BSW, CDU/CSU, FDP, the Greens, Die Linke, SPD and Volt, and answers user questions while citing the original manifesto passages as sources. It deliberately issues no voting recommendations, only presenting and comparing party positions, and the project is open source on GitHub (fhswf/wahl-o-chat). It illustrates how RAG over official documents can support political education while keeping answers traceable to primary texts.
aiDemocracyAngle: An academic, open-source RAG chatbot over party manifestos that shows the traceable-sourcing pattern for trustworthy AI voter assistance.

name: Wahl-O-Mat
tagline: Germany's flagship classic VAA: 38 theses match voters to parties, run by the bpb
description: Wahl-O-Mat is Germany's flagship voting advice application, launched in 2002 and operated by the Federal Agency for Civic Education (bpb). For each election it presents 38 theses on current policy issues; users respond agree/neutral/disagree, optionally weight topics, and receive a ranking of how closely parties match their positions. The theses are drafted by a workshop team of young voters aged 18-26 supported by academics, statisticians and educators, and every participating party answers and explains its own positions. It covers federal, state and European Parliament elections and has been used tens of millions of times per election, making it one of the most-used civic tools in Europe. It is a classic questionnaire VAA rather than an AI system, prized for its neutral, transparent methodology.
aiDemocracyAngle: The reference-standard classic VAA that AI-based tools like wahl.chat and ElectOMate explicitly position themselves against and build upon.
funders: German Federal Agency for Civic Education (bpb)

name: WahlSwiper / VoteSwiper
tagline: Tinder-style swipe VAA for German and European elections, run by a nonprofit association
description: VoteSwiper, known in Germany as WahlSwiper, is a Tinder-style voting advice app for iOS, Android and web, originally built by the Berlin studio MOVACT (founders Max Mitschke, Steven Siebert and Matthias Bannert) and now run as a nonprofit association (Verein). First launched for Germany's 2017 federal election, users swipe left or right on political statements and receive a percentage match with parties that answered the same catalogue; short videos and explanations accompany many questions. Content is developed with political scientists, most recently a team at the University of Freiburg led by Uwe Wagschal. Since the 2019 European elections it has expanded to multiple countries and languages, including English, Turkish, Russian, Arabic and Persian, and has passed a million users. It is a classic questionnaire VAA with a gamified, mobile-first interface rather than an AI system.
aiDemocracyAngle: A gamified, multilingual classic VAA; its swipe UX and open codebase make it a common baseline for the field, though matching is rule-based, not AI.

name: Wahltraut
tagline: Feminist alternative to the Wahl-O-Mat focused on gender equality
description: Wahltraut is a feminist alternative to Germany's Wahl-O-Mat, first launched for the 2021 federal election and updated for 2025 by the #stattblumen initiative (Cordelia Röders-Arnold and Sally Lisa Starken), with theses developed together with the German Women's Council (Deutscher Frauenrat). It works like a standard VAA (users take positions on around 32 statements and get a party ranking) but focuses squarely on gender equality, examining party manifestos on issues such as equal pay, LGBTQIA+ rights, anti-racism and inclusion. Where mainstream VAAs treat feminist policy as one topic among many, Wahltraut makes it the entire lens. It is a classic questionnaire VAA with a thematic focus rather than an AI system.
aiDemocracyAngle: Shows how the classic VAA format is being re-cut around specific values (here, feminism), a design axis AI voter tools can also adopt.

name: Windfall Trust
tagline: Policy research preparing for AI-driven economic disruption and benefit sharing
description: The Windfall Trust is a nonprofit research organization established in 2025 as an independent 501(c)(3), led by founder and CEO Adrian Brown (formerly of the Centre for Public Impact), co-founder Anna Yelizarova and Director of Research Deric Cheng, focused on the economic dimension of AI power concentration. It researches how societies can prepare for AI-driven economic disruption and distribute AI's gains broadly, from scenario planning to a catalog of 48+ policy options for benefit distribution. The work responds to the risk that AI's gains are captured by a small elite of firms and nations while displacement costs fall on workers everywhere, entrenching inequality and undermining the material basis of democratic power. Windfall Trust convenes workshops with the Simon Institute and others to explore benefit-sharing and redistribution pathways for the AI transition.
aiDemocracyAngle: Targets the economic engine of power concentration: pre-commitments and institutions to redistribute AI windfalls before wealth and power ossify in a few hands.

name: WITNESS
tagline: Human-rights defense against deepfakes and synthetic media
description: WITNESS is a human-rights nonprofit founded in 1992 (co-founded by musician Peter Gabriel) that helps people use video and technology to defend human rights. Long led by executive director Sam Gregory, who departed in 2026, its Prepare, Don't Panic initiative, running since 2018, was the first civil-society effort to tackle the threats that deepfakes and generative AI pose to trust in audiovisual evidence and to freedom of expression, centering the needs of journalists and human-rights defenders in the Global Majority. Since 2023 its Deepfake Rapid Response Force provides real-time expert analysis of suspected manipulated media in election and conflict settings worldwide. WITNESS advocates for provenance and authenticity infrastructure (such as content credentials) that protects the vulnerable rather than surveilling them, testifies to lawmakers, and studies AI's impact on democracy in elections from the Philippines to the US.
aiDemocracyAngle: Protects elections and human-rights evidence from AI-driven falsification, giving frontline journalists and defenders tools to verify media.

keyProjects.name: Prepare, Don't Panic
keyProjects.note: Civil-society program on synthetic media threats

name: Yle Vaalikone
tagline: Finnish public broadcaster's VAA matching voters to 18,000+ candidates
description: Vaalikone ('election machine') is the voting advice application of Yle, Finland's public broadcaster, first launched in 1996 and among the most influential VAAs in a country where such tools are mainstream. For each election it asks voters roughly 30 questions across themes like values, education, money and care; candidates answer the same questions on a five-point scale, and the tool matches voters to individual candidates in their district as well as parties. For the 2025 county and municipal elections it carried responses from over 18,000 candidates and was offered in eight languages, including Finnish, Swedish, Sámi, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Somali and English. It is a classic candidate-level questionnaire VAA operated by a major media organisation, not an AI system.
aiDemocracyAngle: A public-broadcaster VAA with mass reach and candidate-level matching; Finnish VAAs like it also seed open-source efforts such as OpenVAA.
